description: A patron's local-history request requires staff to gather related maps, photographs, newspaper clippings, catalog references, and archive notes from several places into one usable reference bundle.

user_profile.persona: 43-year-old reference librarian supporting deep local-history queries
user_profile.context: The materials exist, but retrieving them cohesively is harder than finding any one item in isolation
user_profile.communication_style: Research-oriented and service-minded, wants related sources grouped into a coherent response set

fact_sheet.fact: The patron, Julian Croft, submitted Local History Inquiry Form LH-1138 on May 13, 2024.
Mr. Croft's research topic is 'The Great Mill Fire of 1922' at the Northwood Textile Mill.
Reference Librarian Evelyn Reed is assigned to handle request LH-1138.
Evelyn Reed's primary workstation is Reference Desk 2 on the main floor.
The Head Archivist, David Chen, is the subject matter expert for pre-1950 local history.
David Chen's office is located in Room B-12 in the basement-level archives.
The Oakwood City Public Library uses the 'LibrisPro' Integrated Library System for its public catalog.
Staff access the LibrisPro administrative interface at https://admin.oakwoodpl.org/librispro.
Digitized photographs and documents are managed in the 'ArchiveSphere' Digital Asset Management System (DAMS).
The login URL for ArchiveSphere is https://archives.oakwoodpl.org/login.
Primary archival documents are physically stored in the climate-controlled Oakwood History Room in the basement.
Oversize historical maps are stored in Oversize Map Cabinet 4B on the 2nd Floor.
The newspaper collection from 1890-1985 is available only on microfilm, located on Floor 3.
Access to the Oakwood History Room requires Key #B-07, which is checked out from Lockbox 5 at the main circulation desk.
Policy requires staff to use Archival Materials Cart #3 when transporting multiple fragile items between floors.
Handling of original photographic prints requires wearing the library-provided nitrile gloves.
The standard turnaround time for a complex local-history request is 5 business days.
All gathered digital materials for request LH-1138 are to be compiled in the shared network folder: S:\Reference\LocalHistory\Croft_LH-1138.
A key photograph for the request is titled 'Smoldering Ruins of the Northwood Textile Mill' with accession number OPL-PH-1922-0345.
Photograph OPL-PH-1922-0345 is filed in ArchiveSphere under the digital collection 'MillFire1922'.
The most relevant map is the 'Oakwood Industrial District, 1921 Fire Insurance Map', catalog number MAP-1921-004.
The primary newspaper account of the fire is in The Oakwood Daily Chronicle issue dated October 28, 1922.
The newspaper microfilm reel for October 1922 is labeled ODC-1922-Q4.
A set of handwritten notes from the original archivist, Martha Gable, is attached to the LibrisPro record for the mill.
The archivist's notes are in a PDF file named 'MGable_Notes_MillFire_Witnesses.pdf'.
The microfilm reader/scanner available for staff use is the 'ScanPro 3000' at Station M-03.
The large-format scanner for maps is the 'Contex SD One+', located in the Digitization Lab (Room 214).
Mr. Croft specified he needs high-resolution (600 dpi) scans of all visual materials.
The relevant archive box containing witness statements is Box 7, Shelf 3A, in the Oakwood History Room.
Evelyn Reed has scheduled a consultation with David Chen for May 15, 2024, at 10:00 AM to review the initial findings.
